subject: Performance playbook + MAP: model-variant synthesis & close schedule
messages:
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.inference.com>
To: Chris Turner <chris.turner@helixhealth.com>
Cc: rishi.malhotra@redwood.inference.com, jasmine.liu@redwood.inference.com, tessa.morgan@redwood.inference.com
Date: Tue, 20 Jan 2026 09:10:00 -0800
Subject: Performance playbook + MAP: model-variant synthesis & close schedule

Chris —

Thanks again for the demo last week. As discussed, attached is the mutual action plan (MAP) focused specifically on the performance and model-variant evaluation work we agreed is critical for Helix’s summarization pipeline. High level objective: validate a model variant that meets your latency/throughput SLOs while preserving extraction fidelity for clinical discharge summaries.

Key KPIs (target acceptance criteria)
- Latency: p95 generation latency <= 300ms (end-to-end) for 1k-token budget; p50 <= 90ms
- TTFT (time-to-first-token): <= 80ms for warmed KV cache
- Throughput: baseline 120 requests/sec at concurrency 20 (tokens/sec scaled per average request size)
- Concurrency envelope: stable perf at 1/5/20/50 concurrent streams
- Quality: extractive F1 >= 0.88 on Helix test set; hallucination rate < 2% (human-eval sampled)

Benchmark plan (what Redwood will run)
1) Test matrix across 4 variants: redwood-1.0-7b, redwood-1.1-13b, redwood-quant8-13b, community-13b-llama-quant
2) Measurements: cold start vs warmed cache, p50/p95 latency, TTFT, max sustainable throughput, memory footprint, and token-cost estimates
3) Quality evaluation: automatic metrics (F1/ROUGE-L), then human-in-the-loop sampling (50 cases/variant) for hallucination & instruction-following
4) Environment: Dedicated trial on Redwood Dedicated (us-west) to mirror your on-prem latency envelope; we’ll provide a scoped VPC tunnel for dataset upload

Mutual action items & timeline
- By Jan 27: Helix to provide 200 de-identified sample records (CSV) + representative prompt set and a short acceptance rubric for hallucination. (Action: Chris)
- By Feb 3: Redwood to deliver baseline perf matrix and initial quality summary (automatic metrics). (Action: Monica/Jasmine)
- Feb 3–Feb 17: POC runs, human evals, and two deep-dive syncs (weekly). (Both)
- Target contract signature: Feb 26 (aiming to align with your Q1 procurement window).

Attachments: MAP-Helix-Performance-Plan.xlsx (detailed task list), helix_sample_prompts.csv (example prompts)

If that timeline looks OK I’ll lock the calendar invites and Jasmine will reach out with the harness and access instructions.

Thanks,
Monica Patel
Sr. Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
monica.patel@redwood.inference.com

From: Chris Turner <chris.turner@helixhealth.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.inference.com>
Cc: procurement@helixhealth.com
Date: Tue, 20 Jan 2026 11:45:00 -0600
Subject: Re: Performance playbook + MAP: model-variant synthesis & close schedule

Monica —

Appreciate the clear plan. A few quick clarifying Qs from our side before we assemble the sample data:
- Can you confirm whether the Dedicated trial will include NVMe-backed instance storage for caching? We want to mirror production I/O.
- Pricing: what are the guardrails for the trial in terms of compute hours and data egress? Procurement will need a soft cap to avoid surprises.
- For the human evals: can Redwood run them on our de-identified docs or do you require a separate subset to be uploaded to your test environment?

Procurement is looped in — they’ll want SOC 2 and any standard security artifacts before enabling the tunnel. I can get you the sample CSV by Tuesday next week (Jan 27).

—Chris
Chris Turner
Head of ML Engineering | HelixHealth
chris.turner@helixhealth.com

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.inference.com>
To: Chris Turner <chris.turner@helixhealth.com>
Cc: rishi.malhotra@redwood.inference.com, jasmine.liu@redwood.inference.com
Date: Wed, 21 Jan 2026 08:20:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Performance playbook + MAP: model-variant synthesis & close schedule

Chris —

Answers inline:
- Dedicated trial: yes — we can provision NVMe-backed nodes for the workload. I’ll mark that in the MAP as a must-have for parity testing.
- Trial caps: we’ll provide a complimentary 200 compute-hour window + 10GB egress for the POC. If you want more headroom we can include a short addendum in the trial agreement.
- Human evals: we can run the human sampling either in your environment (if you prefer to keep data inside Helix cloud) or on a Redwood-isolated evaluation environment under the same security controls. Let us know your preference — either works.

Next steps: I’ll update the MAP to reflect NVMe nodes and the trial cap, then Jasmine will send the harness + service-account instructions. Rishi, can you prepare the trial agreement and a short non-binding pricing sheet for procurement?

Thanks,
Monica

From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.inference.com>
To: Chris Turner <chris.turner@helixhealth.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.inference.com>, rishi.malhotra@redwood.inference.com
Date: Thu, 22 Jan 2026 10:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Performance playbook + MAP: model-variant synthesis & close schedule

Chris —

Following up with the technical runbook for the benchmark harness (short version). We’ll run two phases: a micro-benchmark (latency/TTFT) and a throughput soak. Deliverables: CSV per-variant with p50/p95/mean TTFT, p50/p95 latency, throughput @ conc [1,5,20,50], memory & GPU utilization traces, and token-cost estimate.

What we need from you
- S3 or secure Share link with 200 de-identified sample records (CSV): columns = {record_id, raw_text, expected_extracts} — please remove PHI.
- A service account (IAM) or short-lived pre-signed upload token so we can stage data into the trial VPC.
- Representative prompt templates and any temperature/top-k constraints you want exercised.

Quick example commands (we’ll provide a wrapper but here’s the core):
- warm-run to populate KV: redwood-cli perf --model redwood-1.1-13b --warm 50 --input samples.csv
- latency sweep: redwood-cli perf --model $VAR --mode latency --concurrency 1 --requests 500
- throughput soak: redwood-cli perf --model $VAR --mode throughput --concurrency 20 --duration 1800

Timing: once we have the dataset (by Jan 27) we can stand up the trial and deliver baseline results by Feb 3. For the human evals we’ll ask for a 1–2 hour SME session to adjudicate 50 sample outputs per variant.

Attaching the harness README to the MAP. If you prefer we can do the human eval in your environment — in which case we’ll provide the evaluation UI as a container image.

Thanks,
Jasmine Liu
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

From: procurement@helixhealth.com
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.inference.com>, rishi.malhotra@redwood.inference.com
Cc: Chris Turner <chris.turner@helixhealth.com>
Date: Fri, 23 Jan 2026 15:30:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Performance playbook + MAP: model-variant synthesis & close schedule

Monica / Rishi —

Procurement here. Before we move forward with tunnel access and the Dedicated trial we need the following documentation: SOC 2 Type II report, data processing addendum (DPA) draft, and an outline of retention/deletion controls for customer-provided data. Please also confirm trial support hours and the escalation path for incidents during the POC.

We are targeting a paperwork window that aligns with our Feb 26 signature target. Please send the requested artifacts (or links) by EOD Jan 29 so we can queue legal review.

Thanks,
Helix Procurement
procurement@helixhealth.com
